items.title: The hiring funnel, end to end
items.content:
# The hiring funnel, end to end

From the moment headcount is authorised to a signed contract or a closed search, with the actor who owns each step and what the candidate can see from where they stand.
items.summary: From the moment headcount is authorised to a signed contract or a closed search, with the actor who owns each step and what the candidate can see from where they stand.
items.subject: a requisition and the candidate moving through it

states.title: Requisition drafted
states.description: A manager writes the role. Level, band and requirements are decided here, usually by copying the last search for the same team.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing. The role does not exist publicly yet.

states.title: Headcount authorised
states.description: Finance and leadership commit budget against the requisition. Approval can lapse or be withdrawn later without the funnel noticing.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing.

states.title: Posting live
states.description: The role is public. It may also be refreshed automatically every thirty days, which looks identical to a new opening.
states.visible_to_candidate: The posting, and whatever the posting chose to disclose.

states.title: Application received
states.description: A record exists and is linked to the requisition. Nothing has been read.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation, or silence.

states.title: Automated screen
states.description: Parser extraction, keyword thresholds, knockout rules and ranking. Decided in under a second.
states.visible_to_candidate: Either nothing, or a rejection within minutes.

states.title: In the recruiter queue
states.description: Waiting to be read by a person, against an inbound queue that is usually larger than the week has hours for.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, of an indeterminate length.

states.title: Recruiter screen
states.description: A conversation about compensation, timeline, location and a two-minute version of the last project.
states.visible_to_candidate: The call itself, and whichever parameters the recruiter chose to share.

states.title: Technical assessment
states.description: A live exercise, a take-home, or both, scored against a rubric the candidate does not see.
states.visible_to_candidate: The exercise, and sometimes structured feedback afterwards.

states.title: Manager and team panel
states.description: Depth, ownership and collaboration, assessed across several interviewers who may be measuring different things.
states.visible_to_candidate: The conversations. Rarely the scores.

states.title: Compensation and levelling
states.description: The level the panel assigned meets the band finance approved. First time the two are compared.
states.visible_to_candidate: A number, or a renegotiation.

states.title: Offer approval
states.description: Manager, director, finance and the talent committee sign off in sequence. Everyone the candidate met has already said yes.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, usually described as "final checks".

states.title: Offer issued
states.description: A written offer exists. The requisition is still open until the countersignature lands.
states.visible_to_candidate: The offer document.

states.title: Reference and background check
states.description: A third-party record is compared against what the candidate claimed.
states.visible_to_candidate: A request for documents, or nothing.

states.title: Hired
states.description: Contract executed both ways, start date set, onboarding triggered.
states.visible_to_candidate: A signed contract.

states.title: Rejected
states.description: A decision was made and communicated. What it says about the cause is a separate question entirely.
states.visible_to_candidate: A message, ranging from a rubric category to a template.

states.title: Search frozen or cancelled
states.description: Budget withdrawn or the requisition put on hold. Can happen at any point, including after an offer.
states.visible_to_candidate: If the candidate is lucky, an explanation. Often the posting simply disappears.

states.title: Lapsed without a decision
states.description: No one decided anything. The record aged past a threshold, or the posting was never taken down.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, then possibly a bulk rejection at two in the morning.

transitions.label: budget signed off
transitions.guard: Finance commits headcount against the requisition.

transitions.label: posting goes live
transitions.guard: An approved requisition with a written description is published.

transitions.label: application submitted
transitions.guard: The candidate applies, or answers outbound outreach.

transitions.label: rules evaluated
transitions.guard: The record is complete enough for the configured rules to run.

transitions.label: thresholds cleared
transitions.guard: Extraction score and every knockout rule pass.

transitions.label: filtered out
transitions.guard: Any knockout rule fails, or the ranking falls below the advance threshold.

transitions.label: short-listed
transitions.guard: A person reads the profile and puts it on the list.

transitions.label: aged out
transitions.guard: No review happened before the expiry threshold.

transitions.label: parameters align
transitions.guard: Expectations, timeline and location are compatible, and the profile is submitted to the team.

transitions.label: parameters do not align
transitions.guard: Compensation, level, location or availability rules the candidate out before any engineering is discussed.

transitions.label: assessment passed
transitions.guard: The score clears the rubric threshold.

transitions.label: assessment not passed
transitions.guard: The score falls short, or the review was too shallow to find what was there.

transitions.label: panel recommends hire
transitions.guard: Consensus reaches the hire threshold.

transitions.label: panel does not reach consensus
transitions.guard: A split panel under a unanimity rule defaults to no hire.

transitions.label: level and band reconcile
transitions.guard: The assigned level and the approved band overlap.

transitions.label: level and band do not reconcile
transitions.guard: Expectation sits outside the band and neither the level nor the number moves.

transitions.label: sign-off complete
transitions.guard: Every approver in the chain has cleared it.

transitions.label: headcount withdrawn
transitions.guard: Budget is pulled or a freeze is announced before the offer is issued.

transitions.label: offer accepted
transitions.guard: The candidate signs and the checks begin.

transitions.label: offer retracted
transitions.guard: A freeze reaches an outstanding offer before the countersignature.

transitions.label: checks clear
transitions.guard: No unresolved discrepancy in the third-party record.

transitions.label: discrepancy unresolved
transitions.guard: A record mismatch or an eligibility bar is not reconciled.

transitions.label: posting outlives the search
transitions.guard: Hiring stops but the listing is never withdrawn.

transitions.label: requisition reopened
transitions.guard: The search restarts, sometimes with a revised profile, sometimes as an automatic refresh.

items.title: An application inside the ATS
items.content:
# An application inside the ATS

The machine the candidate never sees: what happens to a submitted application between the form and a human being, and the four ways it can end without anyone reading it.
items.summary: The machine the candidate never sees: what happens to a submitted application between the form and a human being, and the four ways it can end without anyone reading it.
items.subject: one application record

states.title: Submitted
states.description: A form post has been accepted. Fields are validated against the requisition schema; nothing has been interpreted.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation page, sometimes an acknowledgement email.

states.title: Parsing
states.description: The document is converted to structured fields. Multi-column layouts, graphics and custom fonts routinely lose whole sections silently.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing.

states.title: Rule evaluation
states.description: Knockout rules, keyword coverage, years thresholds and ranking features run in sequence, short-circuiting on the first failure.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing, for a second or two.

states.title: Queued for human review
states.description: The record is above the threshold and waiting. Queue position depends on source: outbound lists are usually read first.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence. This is where most of the waiting happens.

states.title: Read by a person
states.description: A recruiter opens the profile. The median attention available per profile is measured in seconds when the queue is deep.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing yet.

states.title: Advanced to the funnel
states.description: The record leaves this machine and enters WF-001 at the recruiter screen.
states.visible_to_candidate: An invitation to talk.

states.title: Rejected by rule
states.description: A rule failed. The notification is often queued and sent minutes later, which is what produces a rejection at midnight.
states.visible_to_candidate: A rejection email, minutes after applying.

states.title: Rejected by a person
states.description: Someone read it and passed. What the message says about why is a separate decision, usually a template.
states.visible_to_candidate: A rejection message, generic unless a feedback policy exists.

states.title: Expired unreviewed
states.description: A scheduled job closed the record after a threshold. Nobody read it, and the email it sends is indistinguishable from one that followed a review.
states.visible_to_candidate: A bulk rejection, or nothing at all.

transitions.label: document accepted
transitions.guard: Required fields validate and the file is a supported type.

transitions.label: fields extracted
transitions.guard: Extraction completes, whether or not it recovered the work history.

transitions.label: all rules pass
transitions.guard: Every knockout rule passes and the rank clears the advance threshold.

transitions.label: a rule fails
transitions.guard: Any knockout rule fails, or the ranking falls below the threshold.

transitions.label: a recruiter opens it
transitions.guard: Capacity reaches this position in the queue before the expiry threshold.

transitions.label: threshold reached first
transitions.guard: The record ages past the configured limit with no review recorded.

transitions.label: short-listed
transitions.guard: The profile is put on the active list for outreach.

transitions.label: passed over
transitions.guard: The recruiter decides not to advance it.

items.title: The path as it is supposed to run
items.content:
# The path as it is supposed to run

This is the canonical path: one opening, from a real need to a decision the
candidate can act on. It is written as a machine because that is how the rest of
the registry is written, and because a commitment that cannot be expressed as a
state and a guard is usually not a commitment.

**It is a construct, not a description of anybody.** No employer runs exactly
this. It is assembled from the things employers already say they do — bands on
postings, rubrics agreed before interviews, decisions inside a stated window,
postings taken down when a search ends — and put in one order so that the rest
of the atlas has something to be measured against.

That is the whole point of it. A barrier is not simply a gate: a gate is normal
and this path has fourteen of them. A barrier is the point at which one of these
commitments stops being kept. `deviations` on each state names which ones, which
is why every barrier in the registry appears on exactly one state of this path
and every mechanism on at least one.

Two things this path deliberately does **not** treat as deviations. A decline is
not a deviation — most candidates are declined, and a path that could only end
in a hire would be a fantasy rather than a standard. A closed search is not a
deviation either; needs change and budgets go. What makes both of them part of
the path rather than departures from it is that they arrive, they say what
happened, and they arrive in time to be useful.
items.summary: One opening, from a real need to a decision the candidate can act on, with each step written as the commitment it is supposed to keep. Every barrier in the registry is a place where one of these commitments stops being kept.
items.subject: one opening, and one candidate moving through it

states.title: A real opening, described honestly
states.description: The requisition describes work that exists now, at a level the team actually needs, inside a band the budget already covers. Nothing here is aspirational: the list of requirements is what the job uses, not what the last four candidates happened to have.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing yet. Everything downstream inherits whatever is decided here.

states.title: Published with its terms on the page
states.description: The posting states the compensation band, the location rules, the stages the process has and roughly how long each takes. It comes down when the search ends.
states.visible_to_candidate: The role, the band, the stages, and a date by which the first answer should arrive.

states.title: Applied, and told so
states.description: The application is submitted and acknowledged. The record holds what the candidate actually wrote, and the candidate can tell that it arrived.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation that names the role and says what happens next.

states.title: Machine work stays mechanical
states.description: Automation deduplicates, extracts and orders. It does not decide. Where a rule does end an application, the rule is stated and it is one a person would defend out loud.
states.visible_to_candidate: If a rule ends it here, which rule.

states.title: Read by a person, inside the stated window
states.description: Every application that clears the mechanical stage is read by someone, and read before the window the posting promised runs out.
states.visible_to_candidate: Either a next step or a decision, by the date the posting gave.

states.title: Terms compared before anyone spends time
states.description: Band, level, location, notice period and start date are put side by side in the first conversation, before any assessment is scheduled. Either side can stop here at no cost to the other.
states.visible_to_candidate: The numbers and the constraints, from both sides, in the first call.

states.title: Assessed on the work, against a rubric that is shared
states.description: One timeboxed exercise that resembles the job. The candidate is given the criteria before starting, the timebox is enforced against the evaluator as well, and the same rubric scores everyone.
states.visible_to_candidate: The exercise, the timebox and the criteria — before starting, not after.

states.title: One panel, one question each, one decision rule
states.description: Every interviewer knows what they are measuring and that nobody else is measuring it. The rule that turns their scores into a decision is agreed before the first conversation, and no round is added after the process has started.
states.visible_to_candidate: Who they will meet, what each conversation is for, and how many there are.

states.title: The level meets the band that was published
states.description: The level follows from the evidence the panel gathered, and the band was public from the first day. Reconciling them is arithmetic, not a negotiation about whether the band exists.
states.visible_to_candidate: The same band the posting stated, and which point in it the offer sits at.

states.title: Approval already exists
states.description: Headcount was signed before the role was published, so this step is a countersignature rather than a second decision. If the budget goes, the search closes and everyone inside it is told.
states.visible_to_candidate: A date for the offer, rather than an indefinite period described as final checks.

states.title: A written offer with everything in it
states.description: Salary, level, title, location terms, start date and anything conditional, in writing, with a decision window the candidate agreed to. Nothing in it changes after acceptance.
states.visible_to_candidate: The complete offer document, and how long they have to answer.

states.title: Checks that are proportionate and answerable
states.description: Only the checks the role actually requires. Where a third-party record disagrees with what the candidate said, the discrepancy is put to the candidate before it decides anything.
states.visible_to_candidate: What is being checked, and any discrepancy, before it is acted on.

states.title: Hired on the terms that were published
states.description: Contract executed both ways on the terms that were on the page from the beginning, with a start date both sides chose.
states.visible_to_candidate: A signed contract that matches the posting.

states.title: Declined, with a reason that can be acted on
states.description: Not every candidate is hired, and a decline is not a deviation. What makes it part of this path is that it arrives, it names the stage it happened at and the criterion that decided it, and it says whether applying again is worth anything.
states.visible_to_candidate: Which stage, which criterion, and whether to apply again.

states.title: Search closed, and everyone told
states.description: A search can legitimately stop: the need changes, the budget goes, someone internal turns out to be right for it. What this path requires is that the posting comes down and every candidate still inside the process is told within days.
states.visible_to_candidate: A message saying the search ended, and when.

transitions.label: posted with its terms
transitions.guard: An approved requisition, a band and a described process go live together.

transitions.label: application submitted
transitions.guard: The candidate applies against terms they could read beforehand.

transitions.label: record processed
transitions.guard: The submission is parsed and acknowledged.

transitions.label: passed to a person
transitions.guard: No automated rule ended it, so a person now has it.

transitions.label: worth a conversation
transitions.guard: A person read the profile and wants to talk.

transitions.label: terms are compatible
transitions.guard: Band, level, location and timing work for both sides, said out loud.

transitions.label: work meets the rubric
transitions.guard: The exercise was scored against the criteria the candidate was given.

transitions.label: panel decides by its rule
transitions.guard: The agreed decision rule returns a hire.

transitions.label: level lands inside the band
transitions.guard: The evidence-assigned level maps to a point in the published band.

transitions.label: countersigned
transitions.guard: The approval that existed before publication is confirmed.

transitions.label: offer accepted
transitions.guard: The candidate accepts a complete written offer inside the agreed window.

transitions.label: checks clear
transitions.guard: Nothing proportionate to the role is unresolved.

transitions.label: declined after reading
transitions.guard: A person decided no, and said at which stage and on what criterion.

transitions.label: terms are incompatible
transitions.guard: The gap is named in the same conversation, before any assessment is booked.

transitions.label: work did not meet the rubric
transitions.guard: The score is below the shared criteria, and the criterion is named.

transitions.label: decision rule returns no hire
transitions.guard: The rule agreed beforehand returns no hire, and which dimension decided it is stated.

transitions.label: level and expectation do not meet
transitions.guard: The published band and the candidate's stated expectation do not overlap, which both sides already knew.

transitions.label: discrepancy stands
transitions.guard: The candidate was shown the discrepancy and it remains unresolved.

transitions.label: need changed
transitions.guard: The work no longer exists, and the posting comes down the same week.

transitions.label: budget withdrawn
transitions.guard: Headcount is pulled, and every candidate in the process is told within days.

transitions.label: offer withdrawn and explained
transitions.guard: An outstanding offer cannot stand, and the candidate is told why, in writing, immediately.
